title: SDK compatibility playbook: streaming ergonomics, retry surface, and deprecation roadmap
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: produce a cross-language playbook and automation to guide customers upgrading from the legacy v1 SDKs to the v2 surface. Focus areas: (1) unified retry primitives and backoff defaults, (2) ergonomic streaming APIs (sync/async iterator patterns), (3) explicit deprecation notices and compatibility shims, and (4) changelog automation + example codemods for Python/TypeScript/Go. Deliverables: playbook doc, three example migration recipes (Python, TS, Go), a compatibility shim library for common breaking changes, automated changelog generation hooks that integrate with our release workflow, and a staged rollout plan with canary tests.
comments: 2025-09-12 Maya Patel: Kickoff meeting notes. Agreed scope: not refactor runtime, focus only on surface compatibility & docs. Prioritize streaming ergonomics and retry defaults because these cause the majority of integration bugs. Action items: prototype shim, draft migration guide, add integration tests that run against hosted API to validate behavior.

2025-09-18 Diego Alvarez: Prototype shim implemented that maps old call signatures to v2 handler. Initial tests for Python and TypeScript added. Observed two behavioral differences: (1) previous SDK implicitly retried on 5xx with exponential jitter; v2 requires explicit RetryPolicy. (2) streaming callbacks in v1 delivered 'partial' tokens immediately; v2 uses server-sent events framing and prefers async iterator consumption. Documented both in the design spec.

2025-09-23 Design review (Lina Zhao): Suggested API surface for streaming iterators — unify on a 'stream()' async iterator that yields events with type: 'token'|'delta'|'end' instead of strings. Accepts an optional 'on_partial' callback for sync-friendly code paths. Outcome: accept iterator-first approach with optional callback compatibility helper.

2025-09-29 Eng review (Roberto Singh): Trade-off: iterator-first API is clearer for modern apps but will break many simple synchronous wrapper uses. Decision: implement a small compatibility wrapper: sync_stream() which wraps the async iterator for sync clients and logs a deprecation warning. Add opt-out env var REDWOOD_SDK_ALLOW_SYNC_STREAM=true for internal testing.

2025-10-02 QA (Hannah Li): Added canary automation that runs migration codemods against 5 customer repos in sandbox. Found two edge cases: (a) users that relied on the previous SDK's implicit retry on 429 must opt-in to new retry behavior; add automated migration note and codemod to insert RetryPolicy with rate_limit backoff. (b) Some Go users relied on blocking 'Stream()' call returning a channel of bytes — codemod will convert to receiving from the returned iterator adapter.
2025-10-03 Diego Alvarez: Draft migration recipe summary included below. Next: finalize changelog automation workflow and submit PR to enable semantic changelog commits for sdk-v2 branch.

Migration recipe (Python):
1) Replace Client.stream_text(..., stream=True) -> Client.stream(..., response_mode=\"events\")
2) If your code consumed callbacks, replace:
   def on_token(t): ...
   client.generate(..., on_token=on_token)
   with:
   async for ev in client.stream(...):
       if ev['type'] == 'token': handle(ev['data'])
3) For sync code, use compatibility: for token in client.sync_stream(...): handle(token)  # wrapper issues DeprecationWarning
4) Add explicit RetryPolicy if you want identical retry behavior from v1:
   retry = RetryPolicy(backoff='exponential', max_attempts=4, status_forcelist=[429,500,502,503])
   client = Client(retry_policy=retry)

Migration recipe (TypeScript):
- v1: sdk.generate({stream: true, onToken})
- v2: for await (const ev of sdk.stream({...})) { if (ev.kind === 'token') onToken(ev.text) }
- Codemod: replace .generate\(\{stream:\s*true,\s*onToken:\s*(\w+)\}\) with an async iterator wrapper that calls the original callback.

Migration recipe (Go):
- v1: r := client.StreamGenerate(ctx, req); for t := range r.C { handle(t) }
- v2: iter := client.Stream(ctx, req); for iter.Next() { ev := iter.Event(); if ev.Kind == Token { handle(ev.Text) } }
- Provide helper: ch := client.StreamToChan(ctx, req) // shim to restore channel semantics (deprecated)

2025-10-03 Maya Patel: Changelog automation approach: Use conventional commits on sdk mono-repo; introduce a lightweight 'changelog-bot' that listens for merged PRs with labels (breaking|feature|fix) and appends structured JSON entries to /changelogs/pending.json. A nightly job composes release notes from pending.json and publishes human-friendly markdown plus machine-readable JSON for the Console. Also add a git-codemod command 'rw-sdk codemod migrate-streaming' scaffolded in tools/ to assist bulk updates.

Follow-ups: (a) finish codemods for TS/Go (Diego), (b) add canary matrix in CI that runs representative customer workloads (Hannah), (c) update SDK quickstarts and snippets in docs (Docs team) — target next cycle for docs refresh.
